title: Quiet on purpose
summary: A good code leaves most buckets empty.

cards.text:
Spikes cost something.
A picture of an edge should wake a few buckets, not all of them.

A code that turns every bucket on a little can still copy the picture.
It just spends water the picture did not need.

question.prompt: Silence in most buckets is a failure.
question.why: Silence is the prediction of a sparse code.
question.simpler: Only the buckets that explain the picture need to tip.

question.prompt: What should a photo of a single edge do?
choices: Empty the buckets that match the edge
question.why: A few features explain the edge. The rest stay quiet.
question.simpler: Cost means most of the crowd does nothing.

recall.question: Should most buckets tip on a simple picture?

deeper.note: Olshausen and Field asked a code to rebuild natural images while staying sparse. Oriented filters fell out.

paper.title: Emergence of simple-cell receptive field properties by learning a sparse code for natural images
paper.section: The objective and the learned receptive fields.

terms.definition: A representation that explains the input with as few active units as possible.
